newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel completes $750 million U.S. bond offering.
newsitem.headline: Israel completes $750 million U.S. bond offering.

text.p: The Israeli government completed a $750 million bond offering in the United States, the Treasury said on Thursday.
The bonds carry a 7.052 percent interest rate and are for 30 years, the Treasury said, adding that the rate was only 0.20 basis points above the rate being paid by the U.S. government.

The Israeli bonds are guaranteed by the U.S. government as part of a six-year programme under which Israel is allowed to borrow up to $10 billion. The United States deducts every year from that the amount it estimates Israel spends on West Bank settlements.
This year the deduction is $60 million.

The issue is the ninth conducted in the framework, which was set up to help Israel finance the absorption of hundreds of thousands of immigrants from the former Soviet Union. With the latest issue, Israel has raised $7.3 billion with U.S. backing.
Treasury sources have said they plan to raise $1.35 billion annually over the next two years, including the $750 million completed today.

In addition, Israel has raised $200 million in Eurobonds, in the framework of a three-year $750 million framework, and $250 million in Yankee bonds - all without U.S. guarantees. The offerings were done to test the waters in preparation for when the U.S. guarantee programme expires at the end of 1998.
